result.summary: This PR makes Bitcoin Core's CMake build require that Cap'n Proto/KJ be built with C++ exception support when IPC is enabled, failing configure with a clear message instead of allowing a silent miscompile. It pins -DKJ_NO_EXCEPTIONS=0 for the depends capnp and native_capnp packages, adds a CheckKjExceptions.cmake module that probes the compiler and the installed libkj, and defines KJ_NO_EXCEPTIONS=0 privately on in-tree IPC targets so headers and library agree. Documentation for FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, macOS, and Unix builds is updated to note the exception-support requirement.
result.problem: IPC's runCatchingExceptions relies on kj::getCaughtExceptionAsKj, which capnp's kj library omits when built with KJ_NO_EXCEPTIONS set. Without this check, a system or self-built libkj lacking exception support can produce IPC binaries that silently misbehave or fail to link late in the build, which the author says is why depends packages and a new build-time check are needed (addresses #36058).

result.card: This PR adds a CMake-time check that fails configure if Cap'n Proto's KJ library lacks C++ exception support, which IPC's runCatchingExceptions silently depends on (missing kj::getCaughtExceptionAsKj). It pins -DKJ_NO_EXCEPTIONS=0 for the depends capnp/native_capnp packages and privately defines the same macro on in-tree IPC and libmultiprocess targets so headers and library agree, addressing RFC issue #36058. The NetBSD doc note that KJ 'can mis-detect this when __has_feature is stubbed' is the strongest evidence this is a real, not just theoretical, footgun on some supported platforms. The PR is draft, has had zero reviewer engagement, and conflicts with the unrelated open PR #32387 (Windows IPC support) on overlapping files, but nothing blocks a code review of the current diff.
